Hourly records give net electrical output (MW) together with ambient temperature (2 to 37 degC), ambient pressure, relative humidity and condenser vacuum. Hourly records give net electrical output (MW) together with ambient temperature (2 to 37 degC), ambient pressure, relative humidity and condenser vacuum. The plant has an inlet evaporative cooler in front of the compressor, which operators run in warm weather. In cold weather the gas turbine reaches the rated limit of its generator, and the control system holds it at that limit. At 15 degC and 1013 mbar the gas turbine alone produces about 343 MW. The gas turbine generator is limited to 364 MW. Operators switch the evaporative cooler on when ambient temperature exceeds about 24 degC.

Hourly records give net electrical output (MW) together with ambient temperature (2 to 37 degC), ambient pressure, relative humidity and condenser vacuum. The plant has an inlet evaporative cooler in front of the compressor, which operators run in warm weather. In cold weather the gas turbine reaches the rated limit of its generator, and the control system holds it at that limit. At 15 degC and 1013 mbar the gas turbine alone produces about 343 MW. The gas turbine generator is limited to 364 MW. Operators switch the evaporative cooler on when ambient temperature exceeds about 24 degC.
Training data available: 146 hourly records with ambient temperature between 19.1 and 21.6 degC. Within these records a linear fit gives d(output)/d(temperature) = -2.15 MW/degC (standard error 0.49). Predictions are needed outside this temperature range.
